title: Power Outage
description: Use this list to prepare for outages and to work through the first hours and days when the power goes out.

sources.title: Be Prepared for a Power Outage
Avoid Foodborne Illness During Temporary Power Outages
What to Do to Protect Yourself During a Power Outage
Winter Storms Aren't Over: CPSC Warns of Deadly Carbon Monoxide Risks and Fires During Power Outages

items.text: Install battery or battery-backup carbon monoxide alarms on every level and near bedrooms, and test them
Run generators, grills, and camp stoves outdoors only, at least 20 feet (6 m) from windows, doors, and vents - never in a garage or on a porch
Never heat the home with a gas oven or stove, and never run a car in a garage
Never plug a generator into house wiring without a proper transfer switch - it can kill utility workers
Make a backup power plan for medical devices (oxygen, CPAP, pumps) and tell your utility if someone depends on one
Know how long refrigerated medicines like insulin can stay at room temperature; keep a cooler and gel packs ready
Flashlights and lanterns with spare batteries for every person - not candles
Keep fridge and freezer doors closed: a closed fridge keeps food safe about 4 hours, a full freezer about 48 hours, a half-full one about 24
Put appliance thermometers in the fridge (40 F / 4 C or below) and freezer (0 F / -18 C or below)
After 4 hours without power, move meat, milk, and leftovers to a cooler with ice; when in doubt, throw it out
Store water: at least 1 gallon (3.8 L) per person per day, and fill extra containers if pumps may lose power
Non-perishable food and a manual can opener for several days
Battery or hand-crank radio for news and alerts
Charged power banks and a car charger for phones
Unplug appliances and electronics to protect them from surges; leave one lamp on to know when power returns
Report the outage to your utility and check if neighbors are out too
Cold weather: close off unused rooms, layer clothing, and go to a warming center if the home gets too cold
Hot weather: stay in the coolest room, drink water often, and go to a cooling center if needed
Check on older neighbors and people living alone at least twice a day
Keep cash in small bills - card readers and ATMs may not work
Know how to open your garage door manually
Bag-lined bucket toilet and supplies in case water pressure fails
When power returns, turn appliances on a few at a time and replace refrigerated medicines that got warm, as the label or pharmacist advises
